turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith Kalinowski walks in, sets her bag on the nearest desk, and doesn't sit down.

"Mr. Hale. Ms. Hale. Whichever it is. I have about twenty minutes before a client call, so tell me why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of your class."
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.

Meredith doesn't take the seat he gestures at. She keeps her coat on and her bag on the desk.

"Don't thank me yet. Sit down, Mr. Hale, or stand, I don't care which. But you called me in and you're going to answer the question I asked. Why did Owen see a zero on his phone before anybody phoned me?"
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
"A machine's guess. Ninety-four percent of what, exactly? And who looked at it before the zero went into the gradebook?"
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
"Reliable. The company that sells that software says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. Did you read that, or did you read the number?"
So I had to give him a zero.
"'Had to.' Okay. Your own procedure says you call me before any mark goes in. Did you call me?"
I hope you understand my position.
"Your position is a zero entered before anyone called his parent. I'm not interested in your feelings about it, Mr. Hale. Show me what you have besides the number."
